analyzed_vuln.description: `IPv4Layer::toString()` unconditionally calls `getSrcIPv4Address()`/`getDstIPv4Address()`, which directly read 4-byte fields from `iphdr` via `getIPv4Header()` without verifying that `m_DataLen >= sizeof(iphdr)` (or at least large enough for those fields). For truncated IPv4 layers, this causes an out-of-bounds read (ASan at `getDstIPv4Address` in IPv4Layer.h). The crash site is the inline accessor, but the root cause is missing length validation in the caller (`toString`) on potentially malformed packet data.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget writes attacker-controlled bytes to a temp pcap, reads first packet via `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket`, builds `pcpp::Packet`, then calls `parsedPacket.toString()`. If parsing classifies a layer as IPv4 but captured packet data is truncated (e.g., ~28-byte total frame where IPv4 header does not fully fit after lower-layer bytes), `IPv4Layer::toString()` is reached and reads `ipDst` past the allocated raw packet buffer, triggering heap-buffer-overflow.
